title: Travel, problems & emergencies
goal: Handle hotels and trains, report a lost item or a problem, call for help, and use 'if… then' sentences.
intro:
This unit prepares you for things going wrong: a delayed train, a lost wallet, an accident or a visit to the police. The key grammar is the conditional **જો … તો** 'if … then', which in Gujarati is very regular.

Emergency numbers in India: **112** (all emergencies), **100** (police), **108** (ambulance — in Gujarat the 108 service is famous and fast).

grammar.title: Real conditions: જો … તો
grammar.body:
'If X, then Y' is **જો X, તો Y**. The **જો** can be dropped in speech, but **તો** almost always appears.

The if-clause uses either the **subjunctive** (Unit 18) or the **future**; the main clause uses the future or an imperative:

**જો વરસાદ પડે, તો અમે નહીં આવીએ** 'If it rains, we won't come'
**જો તમને મોડું થાય, તો ફોન કરજો** 'If you're late, please call'
**જો ટ્રેન રદ થશે, તો બસમાં જઈશું** 'If the train is cancelled, we'll go by bus'

The subjunctive version sounds slightly more hypothetical; the future version more likely. With **હોવું**, the subjunctive is **હોય**: **જો તમારી પાસે સમય હોય તો…** 'if you have time…'

grammar.title: Unreal conditions: 'if I had known…'
grammar.body:
For things that **didn't happen** (counterfactuals), both clauses use the **-ત** form, which does not change for person or gender in standard speech: **હોત** 'would have been', **આવત** 'would have come', **કરત** 'would have done'.

**જો મને ખબર હોત, તો હું આવત** 'If I had known, I would have come'.

You'll also hear the **-તો / -તી** forms used the same way in colloquial speech: **જો મને ખબર હોત તો હું આવતો**.

examples.en: If I had money, I'd buy a car.

dialogue.title: A lost bag at the station
dialogue.setting: Emma has left her bag on a train at Vadodara station and goes to the railway police (GRP) desk.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: માફ કરજો, મારી થેલી ટ્રેનમાં રહી ગઈ.
lines.roman: māf karjo, mārī thelī ṭrenmāṃ rahī gaī.
lines.en: Excuse me, I left my bag on the train.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.en: Don't panic. Which train was it?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.en: The Shatabdi from Mumbai, coach C3.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.native: અમે આગળના સ્ટેશને ફોન કરીએ છીએ. જો થેલી મળશે, તો અહીં પાછી આવશે.
lines.roman: ame āgaḷnā sṭeshane fon karīe chhīe. jo thelī maḷshe, to ahīṃ pāchhī āvshe.
lines.en: We're calling the next station. If the bag is found, it'll come back here.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.native: બે-ત્રણ કલાક. ત્યાં સુધી આ ફરિયાદ ફૉર્મ ભરો.
lines.roman: be-traṇ kalāk. tyāṃ sudhī ā fariyād form bharo.
lines.en: Two or three hours. Meanwhile, fill in this report form.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: આભાર. જો મેં ધ્યાન રાખ્યું હોત, તો આવું ન થાત!
lines.roman: ābhār. jo meṃ dhyān rākhyuṃ hot, to āvuṃ na thāt!
lines.en: Thanks. If I'd been careful, this wouldn't have happened!

culture: Gujarat is generally considered one of India's safer states, and people are quick to help a lost traveller — though directions may be given with more confidence than accuracy, so ask twice. Indian Railways has a Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Government Railway Police (GRP) post at major stations. The phrase **થાય, ચાલે** 'it happens, it's fine' captures a very Gujarati calm in the face of small disasters.

tip.title: Something isn't working
tip.body:
- **X ચાલતું નથી** 'X isn't working' — the ending agrees with X: એસી **ચાલતું** નથી (n), લાઇટ **ચાલતી** નથી (f), પંખો **ચાલતો** નથી (m).
- 'Booked in my name' is **મારા નામે** બુક છે.
- Ask for things with the polite **-શો?**: ચાવી **આપશો?**

sentences.en: The fan in the room isn't working.
The bathroom light isn't working.
This key doesn't work.
Where is my luggage?
May I have your passport, please?
How was your journey?
Our journey was very long.
My luggage is very heavy.
This hotel is close to the station.
Could I have the room key?

lessons.title: At the station

tip.title: If … then: જો … તો
tip.body:
- **જો X, તો Y** = 'if X, (then) Y'. જો can be dropped; **તો** usually stays.
- The 'if' part uses the plain present (**થાય, લાગે**) or the future; the main part uses the future or a request: જો ટ્રેન મોડી **હોય**, **તો** ફોન કરજો.
- **હોવું** becomes **હોય** in the 'if' part: જો ટિકિટ ન **હોય** તો…

tip.title: 'It got lost', 'it got stolen'
tip.body:
- Things 'get lost' or 'get stolen' — the thing is the subject and the verb agrees with it: મારું પાકીટ **ખોવાઈ ગયું** (n), મારી થેલી **ખોવાઈ ગઈ** (f), મારો ફોન **ચોરાઈ ગયો** (m).
- **ચોરી થઈ** 'there's been a theft'.
- At the police station: **મારે ફરિયાદ નોંધાવવી છે** 'I want to file a report'.
tip.pattern: મારું / મારી / મારો + thing + ખોવાઈ ગયું / ગઈ / ગયો

sentences.en: I've lost my bag.

sentences.roman: gaīkāle rātre amārā gharmāṃ chorī thaī.
sentences.en: There was a burglary at our house last night.

tip.title: In an emergency
tip.body:
- Shout **બચાવો!** 'help!' and **કોઈ મદદ કરો!** 'somebody help!'.
- Use plain polite commands: **એમ્બ્યુલન્સ બોલાવો**, **પોલીસને ફોન કરો**, **તરત આવો**.
- 'Someone is hurt' is a feeling-style sentence: **એને ઈજા થઈ છે**.
- In India dial **108** (એકસો આઠ) for an ambulance, **112** for any emergency.

sentences.en: Call a doctor right away!
Call the police.
Please come quickly.
There's been an accident on the road.
He's badly hurt.
The bleeding won't stop.

sentences.native: આગ લાગી છે! બધા બહાર જાઓ!
sentences.roman: āg lāgī chhe! badhā bahār jāo!
sentences.en: There's a fire! Everyone get out!
Help! My dad has fallen!
Is there a clinic nearby?

lessons.title: If only… and staying calm

tip.title: 'If I had known…'
tip.body:
- For things that **didn't** happen, both halves use the **-ત** form: **જો મને ખબર હોત, તો હું આવત** 'if I had known, I would have come'.
- The -ત form never changes: હોત, આવત, કરત, થાત.
- 'I know / don't know' is **મને ખબર છે / નથી**.
- Calm someone: **ગભરાશો નહીં** 'don't panic', **તમે સલામત છો** 'you're safe'.
